public_rationale: The prediction has no deadline. Anthropic reports reduced engineering hiring attributed to AI and increasingly autonomous work, which are meaningful counterevidence to a broad denial of substitution. The records examined do not establish a decisive, corroborated replacement deployment under the stated rule. The forecast therefore remains open; this is not evidence that never is correct.
limitations: A broader reading that includes any avoided hiring would make the company survey more directly contradictory.
The strongest staffing evidence is company-reported.
The assessment does not require the disappearance of the profession or the absence of all human supervision.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Coding LLMs do not and never will replace software engineers because LLMs are inherently unreliable.

statement.excerpt: To Summarize: Coding LLMs Don’t Actually Replace Software Engineers, and Never Will, Due To The Inherent Unreliability Of Large Language Models

from_speaker: Coding LLMs Don’t Actually Replace Software Engineers
Due To The Inherent Unreliability Of Large Language Models
our_interpretation: Replacement means sustained substitution for substantive software-engineering jobs, including demonstrably avoided hiring, rather than just generating code or saving some worker time.
Ordinary human management and review do not automatically disqualify replacement. Evidence must show that humans are not still doing the substantive work attributed to the replacement.
Inherent unreliability is the proposed explanation, not a conditional antecedent that must occur before the forecast can be assessed.
criteria.support_condition: No finite period without replacement can establish the unlimited never prediction.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A documented deployment demonstrates reliable, sustained substitution for substantive software-engineering jobs and verifies the resulting labor substitution.
